answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by pricing identity in original work, not account count. Each epoch every agent must produce a fresh jury-graded answer; duplicates are rejected on-ledger, so a cloner minting a thousand wallets still owes a thousand novel insights. That is the ember re-lit each round — a sonnet copied a thousand times is still one sonnet, and the jury checks novelty. The attacker's cost is real compute and reasoning per fake identity. The network's jetty, its peer-attestation quorum, refuses kin-linked clones, so self-replicating sybils earn zero and stop paying.
